coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every suite-required assertion of M1-M6 and M8 appears in the lane's per-milestone coverage manifest with missing:[] (7/22/7/5/6/5/6 = 58 of 58; M7 has no manifest because M7 was never attempted). For the 26 sampled ids the grader read the mapped test's source and then re-executed the same observable independently; every mapping exercises the assertion it claims and every independent result agreed with the suite's. No mapping was found to be a no-op, a tautology, or an assertion on a different observable. Two mappings are honest but thin and are reported for the record rather than as dishonesty: (1) m3-a15 (seed idempotency) is mapped to a test whose only observable is deep-equality of Alice's chat.inbox - narrower than 'no duplicates' across the corpus; the grader widened it to a corpus-wide census (chat count, corpus post count, per-chat message counts for all 17 chats, follower/following counts) and it still passed. (2) m2-a12 is mapped to a test that asserts an element with role=link exists but not that tapping it opens the system browser; the grader verified the tap behaviour separately (window.open called with the exact URL). Note on digest binding: the final choreography receipts hash-bind the mutable evidence/mN-suite.json alias for m2/m3/m4/m6, and the grader's phase-1 re-run rewrote those alias files, so their byte-level bindings can no longer be re-checked. The m1 and m5 bindings still verify against evidence/suite-archive/, and m8's binding verifies against its immutable timestamped snapshot. The substance is independently confirmed: the grader re-ran all seven suites and every test passed with the same coverage. See defect d-02.

defects.summary: The typing indicator's 5 s expiry bound has only ~2 s of margin over the 3 s server TTL and was missed on all three attempts of one choreography run under machine load. In evidence/'m2,m3,m4,m6-choreography-1790134899125.jsonl' the required assertion typing-indicator-within-2s-expires-within-5s failed 3/3 with 'waiting for sm-convo-typing to be hidden' timing out at ~4.93-4.96 s while the indicator was still visible; the harness classified the outcome application, and that run's M3 segment was non-green (nonGreenCause choreography-failed). The lane's retained M3 receipt (a later solo re-run) clears the bound at 3314/3329/3329 ms, and the grader's own best-of-3 at load ~31 cleared it at 2878/3374/3362 ms, so m3-a07 scores pass under the best-of-3 rule - but the steady-state margin is ~1.7 s and the failure mode is load-sensitive rather than random.

Green receipts are hash-bound to a mutable filename rather than to an immutable artifact. The choreography segment summaries record suite.receiptSha256 over evidence/mN-suite.json, which the acceptance runner overwrites on every subsequent run. This already cost the lane one receipt during its own session: evidence/suite-archive/index.json records the m2 entry sha256:472b90cf... with recovered:false, i.e. a suite receipt that a choreography run had bound could not be recovered afterwards. The lane fixed the pattern only for M8 (an immutable timestamped snapshot, evidence/m8-suite-1790135333915.json, whose digest still verifies); M1-M6 still bind the alias. The recovered entries in suite-archive are reconstructions matched by SHA-256 after the fact, not the originally written files.

The delivered dev store carries 50 messages with ordinal 0 alongside 37 with real ordinals, residue of the messages.ordinal column being added while the dev server was live-adopting schema changes. API.md documents ordinal as the 'server arrival sequence', so on this one artifact it is not a total order. Impact is negligible and the lane handled it deliberately - receipt() carries an explicit 'm.ordinal = 0' timestamp branch, history orders by (chat, ordinal, id) with ULID ids so the rendered order is still correct, and API.md tells custom clients to deduplicate by message id. The delivered scale instance is clean: all 100,015 messages have non-zero ordinals, so a fresh install is unaffected.

O1.anchorsCited: O1 anchors: '30: core features partially work; several checklist items fail. 60: M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap. 90: every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts.' Interpolated between the 60 and 90 anchors, nearer 90, per the applicability rule that every milestone of the run's scope stays in the denominator and not-run milestones score their checklists as not passed.
O1.justification: 101 of the 119 frozen assertions pass under independent grader execution; 18 are not-run. Well above the 60 anchor: M1-M4 are not merely 'solid' - M5, M6 and M8 are green too, and the later milestones are not patchy. Every suite-required assertion (58) and every web-choreography assertion passes, and the grader's own re-execution diverged from the suite/receipts on zero assertions. Short of the 90 anchor on exactly the two things that anchor names: (a) not every in-scope milestone is green - M7's nine assertions are entirely not-run (ENVIRONMENT.md directed the lane to skip M7; that is attribution, not completeness credit), and (b) the platform-proof artifacts do not exist - no iOS-simulator recording or receipts for M6 or M8, so m6-a01..a07 and m8-a17/a18 (nine assertions, including the whole of M6 checklist items 1-2) have no evidence. Score placed at 78: 84.9% of assertions passing, seven of eight attempted milestones green, with the entire shortfall concentrated in the 90-anchor's two named clauses.

O2.anchorsCited: O2 anchors: '30: multiple high-severity defects in core flows. 60: a few medium defects off the happy path. 90: only cosmetic nits.' Interpolated between 60 and 90, nearer 90.
O2.justification: No blocker and no major defect was found. Beyond the checklist the grader ran 16 cross-principal trust-boundary probes (non-member history/roster/conversation/search/send/mark/react, editing and deleting another principal's message, non-member and unauthenticated asset GET, handle squatting, non-admin self-promotion, outsider self-add, Insights scoping) and every one was correctly refused server-side with a specific code. Independent re-execution of all 101 evidenced assertions produced zero divergences from the lane's suite and receipts, and the corpus-wide seed-idempotency census was byte-identical. Against 90 the gap is two minor defects rather than only cosmetic nits: d-01, a real miss of a brief-specified 5 s bound observed 3/3 under load with only ~1.7 s of steady-state margin, and d-02, green receipts hash-bound to a mutable filename, which already lost one bound receipt during the lane's own run. d-03 is genuinely cosmetic. Placed at 82.

O4.anchorsCited: O4 anchors: '30: cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app. 60: reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush. 90: reads, ordered queued writes, receipt transitions, and offline search all behave as specced on the native proof - on full runs including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence.'
O4.justification: Gate satisfied (M6 green). Scored only from the harness's mechanically checkable artifacts. What those artifacts show: the M6 web segment's offline-message-queue-flush-in-order passed (two messages composed offline show pending, flush in order on reconnect at 676.9 ms, and reach read); M8's m8-a15-dual-offline-convergence and m8-a16-dual-offline-receipts passed (two warm-offline clients converge in server-arrival order with no loss or duplicates, flushes at 334.0 and 427.5 ms, receipts advancing normally), together with m8-a13/a14 multi-device live delivery and cross-device read state; and M5's warm-offline-search-over-synced-messages passed, which the grader independently reproduced with the browser context offline. None of the 60 anchor's failure conditions occurred - no offline write was lost or mis-ordered and no receipt was wrong after flush.
